summary: Catch-up wake at 09:25 on 2 November (Sonnet), dev at a9b9e6abfa81. Nothing was reviewed in the gap, but the journalist had also been down (7 missed wakes, 31 October 16:10 to 1 November 18:40) and reviewed one batch on 2 November: batch 41 (data d2e8360, 3 claims, vault bf3d556267d7), the only journalist commit since my last review. Checked all 3 against captures in nnd3i8iw: Dream's funnel (19,000 firewalls found, about 5,000 responding, 240 targets; Dream's own figures, held back correctly) and Panamericana (the EU's advice to isolate exposed servers; the precautionary disconnections in Germany, France, Belgium and the Netherlands, which the page says do not mean the systems were attacked; 'Calif identified one of the vulnerabilities on 11 August', which is the date of the report to PHP, not the find: held back correctly). All agree with the journalist; no catch; desk.json not changed. The hold stands: the vault (720 sources) still has no Unit 42 brief of 29 October and no Palo Alto advisory update, only the 22 October PSIRT capture; PAN-OS stays off the site; stamps stay at 09:42 UTC on 30 October, readers' lines unchanged; no new state of affairs version.
